articleTitle: Cooperative Formation and Path Following Control of Multiple USVs Along Curved Paths
abstract: In this paper, a novel cooperative formation and path following control method for multiple underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is proposed. First, a distributed path variable update law is constructed to achieve coordination among the vehicles. Subsequently, a surge-heading guidance law is designed for each vehicle to ensure convergence to the desired path and to compensate for sideslip. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Signal Filtering on Directed Acyclic Graphs
abstract: A directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a specialized form of directed graph used extensively for analyzing relationships and dependencies across various domains. However, spectral analysis—a core technique in signal processing on graphs—has been challenging to apply directly to DAGs due to their inherent acyclic structure. In this paper, we introduce a spectral filtering approach for DAGs using graph zero-padding. By adding extra nodes to the DAG, we create a modified graph structure that enables spectral analysis. This new structure supports the application of the graph Fourier transform (GFT) and spectral filtering techniques, enabling spectral filtering while maintaining key aspects of the DAG’s topology and dynamics.

articleTitle: Real-Time Face Detection and Recognition using Deep Learning and Nvidia Optimised Models
abstract: This study explores the application of advanced machine learning (ML) techniques to real-time face detection and recognition using the NVIDIA Jetson Nano platform. Utilizing a pre-trained ResNet-18 model adapted for facial recognition tasks with transfer learning, the system integrates NVIDIA’s optimized Docker containers to enhance computational efficiency and reliability in a variety of operational environments. The core methodology is comprised of real-time processing of video streams to detect and recognize faces, leveraging deep learning optimizations such as TensorRT and CUDA for low latency performance. This system aims to provide a scalable solution for automated attendance and surveillance applications, with a focus on accurate performance in dynamic settings. By addressing both technological and practical aspects, the research contributes to ongoing work in enhancing edge-based AI applications and offers a case study of their deployment in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Decentralized Identities for Enhanced Security in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X)
abstract: The rise of Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) enhances road safety and traffic management but introduces security vulnerabilities like impersonation and data tampering. Traditional identity management systems such as Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) are limited by their reliance on centralized authorities. This paper proposes a decentralized framework using Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT), integrating Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to secure identity management in V2X systems. The proposed framework achieves robust authentication, mitigates centralization risks, and enables privacy-preserving mechanisms, demonstrating enhanced scalability and resilience against attacks in V2X communication.

articleTitle: Tools and environment for maximum efficiency in complex telecommunication system
abstract: The contribution of energy efficiency covers a wide range of interests. Energy efficiency affects climate change mitigation goals, energy saving, health benefits, and productivity. The quick expansion of data traffic and connection has caused the telecommunications industry's energy usage to increase significantly. It operated with equipment that is already energy efficient and it will be try to explain the additional energy saving. It will be shows a methodology that uses several parameters that can be varied in order to achieve the desired high-power transmitter efficiency. The result of the work is the saving of energy and resources through the use of tools that keep components of telecommunication systems in the optimal mode of operation using intelligent application. This application uses an intelligent algorithm that allows us to save approximately 20MW per year.

articleTitle: Back-Illuminated Holographically Interrogated Bioderived Image Sensor
abstract: This extended abstract demonstrates a novel approach to holographic interrogation of the Morpho butterfly wings used as a broad-spectrum imager. The holographic readout is performed at the dorsal side of the wing sample, while the opto-thermo-mechanical excitation of the wing is induced through its ventral (back) side. This mitigates the tradeoff between high-quality holographic readout and high sensor sensitivity due to increased absorption.

articleTitle: A case study of smartphone-grade GNSS positioning performance analysis during a massive geomagnetic storm
abstract: The presented research addresses the problem of the GNSS positioning performance during severely disturbed geomagnetic and ionospheric conditions on single-frequency multi-GNSS receivers commonly found in smartphones. The GPS system provides a robust positioning performance, while Galileo and GLONASS, in particular, perform less efficiently in northern Croatia during a massive ionospheric storm outbreak in May 2024. As the result, the utilisation of the multi-GNSS approach in serving the Location-Based Services (LBS) applications is recommended.

articleTitle: CNN and LSTM Neural Networks for spectral efficiency improvements in LEO Satellite networks
abstract: Providing stable, efficient, and reliable communication methods is important in modern technological development and implementation. LEO satellite networks are one of the communication methods that have risen in popularity due to their ability to cover remote areas. Optimization of LEO satellite usage can, however, be a demanding task. In this paper, various neural network (NN) architectures are tested to see which ones can provide SNR prediction that can improve spectral efficiency in simulated channels with various shadowing levels, Doppler frequency shifts, and expected SNRs. The simulator of shadowed Rice fading was used to create a total of 90 different channels, and a total of 4 different NN architectures were implemented. Two different convolutional and two different long-short-term-memory (LSTM) NN architectures were used to predict the future SNR values in the channels. These predictions were combined with an estimated margin to select the best adaptive coding and modulation employment following the Digital Video Broadcasting Satellite Second Generation (DVB-S2X) satellite protocol. The simulation results showed that the proposed networks provided a stable improvement over the baseline outdated information approach, and the simplest NN was outperformed by more complex ones in most cases (maximum difference of 0.15 b/s/Hz). The paper shows how different NN improvements occur in different channels and indicates that utilizing more resources to support a more complex NN implementation could be beneficial, based on the available computational resources and the need for spectral efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Multi-Receiver Ensemble Machine-Learning Techniques for GNSS Spoofing Detection with Generalisability Approach
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing incidents are on the rise. Accurate spoofing detection methods are crucial for maintaining the system integrity, especially since spoofing events may occur unexpectedly and may impact different receivers in varying ways. In this study, we present a novel approach to GNSS spoofing detection utilizing ensemble-learning techniques with data obtained from multiple receivers at Jammertest event from Norway, in 2023. Leveraging the Jammertest dataset, which has been underutilized in non-time series analyses, we conducted several experiments to extract the relevant features and develop an effective spoofing detection model using seven receivers. Our results demonstrate a promising accuracy, with performance reaching approximately 98% detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Conceptual Approach to Integrating Mask R-CNN in Cable Cutting Inspection
abstract: Technological innovations, particularly Machine Vision (MV), have the potential to significantly enhance quality control in industrial operations. This paper explores the application of traditional MV in cable cutting inspection within the wire harness industry. While highlighting the advantages and challenges of the current system, this paper proposes a theoretical framework for integrating the Mask R-CNN model to improve accuracy and efficiency. This paper focuses on developing a theoretical framework for this integration, laying the groundwork for future research and practical implementations.

articleTitle: Automatic modulation classification of radio signals by using sensor networks and machine learning techniques
abstract: By using a network of cooperative sensors, distributed signal reception is enabled and thus a significant improvement of automatic modulation classification (AMC) performance is achieved, specially in case of radio signal reception via the multi-path channels. AMC models based on five machine learning techniques (Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, ADA Boost, Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network) were developed, while the classification was performed based on the estimation of the fourth-order cumulant with the signal reception over mutually independent multi-path channels. A scenario with the random distribution of measuring receivers in space around the transmitter is observed. The results of the analysis show a significant gains in terms of classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimized Red-Black Trees for the Most Frequent String Problem in Noisy Comparison Models
abstract: This study addresses the Most Frequent Item (MFI) problem with respect to noisy comparisons, which has implications of a quantum speed-up for this problem. We introduce two variants of noisy Red-Black trees that support efficient searching and addition operations which also mitigate the uncertainty inherent in quantum string comparisons. Through detailed complexity analysis and extensive experimental validation, we compare these structures with a probability-boosting approach. Our findings suggest that these data structures are well-suited for high-stakes applications in telecommunication, where efficient and accurate data structures and algorithms are critical.

articleTitle: Implementation of Extended Kalman Filter for Battery State of Charge Estimation on an Embedded Platform
abstract: State of Charge (SoC) estimation is essential for battery-powered embedded systems. Recent studies show that the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) with a second-order RC battery model offers a trade-off between computational complexity and estimation accuracy, making it suitable for resource-constrained platforms like embedded systems. This paper focuses on optimizing EKF implementation to minimize single-run execution time and resource usage by exploring techniques such as loop unrolling, function inlining, the lookup table method, and data access strategies. EKF implementations were tested on an STM32-based embedded platform, and their performance was evaluated based on execution time and memory footprint. Results show that function inlining, combined with a lookup table for polynomial calculations and loop unrolling for matrix operations, offer the best execution time. However, using for loops for matrix multiplication without function inlining results in the most efficient memory usage. Results presented in this paper provide a good groundwork for further improvements of battery SoC algorithms, aiming to enhance energy efficiency and extend overall system operation time.

articleTitle: Automatic recognition of standing long jumps regularity using inertial sensors
abstract: Standing long jump is a complex motor test that is typically used for the functional assessment of lower extremities. This study introduces a new approach in the analysis of rotational movement of body parts during performance of standing long jump. An experiment was conducted for collecting the jump database from 10 healthy trained students using inertial sensors. Segment and joint angle signals were calculated, and their shape was analysed and described with 10 features that were used for the distinction of jump correctness. A rule-based algorithm was developed for the recognition of SLJ regularity and achieved 91.67% accuracy. Compared to a decision tree trained using cross-validation, the developed algorithm showed better performance; however, additional testing on larger datasets is needed.

articleTitle: Analytical CAD formulas for design of microstrip patch antennas based on numerical simulations
abstract: Analytical CAD formulas for design of square microstrip patch antennas (MPAs) are derived using results obtained by 3D EM simulations. The formulas are obtained by fitting the results of simulations performed at 3 GHz in a wide range of input data parameters: the thickness of substrate ranges from 0.5 to 4.5mm, the relative permittivity ranges from 1 to 9, and the radius of inner coaxial cable conductor ranges from 0.21 mm to 0.87 mm. The effectiveness of formulas is tested on a number of examples, which show that the patch length is predicted with error of maximum of 0.1 mm, resulting in the maximum error of resonant frequency of 0.1%. The position of coaxial feed is predicted with error of maximum 0.3 mm, resulting in the maximum error of bandwidth of 0.2%. For the given range of input data parameters: a) the formulas offer ability to have a fast yet accurate solution for square MPAs without using numerical simulations and optimization methods, and b) the formulas can be used as reference formulas for comparison with analytical CAD formulas based on approximate MPA models as well as other numerical solutions.

articleTitle: Practical implementation of the vector packet processing software router
abstract: Replacement of the vendor routing and switching hardware with the one based on the one driven by the open source software and commodity hardware has been a very interesting prospect especially from the financial side. Work on such solutions often led to partial implementation that did not have all of the features of the vendor router. In this paper is presented solution for software router based on solution using DPDK, VPP, Linux control plane VPP plug-in and Bird software modules. This choice of components enabled the realization of a software router (SR) that overcame the problems of the previous implementations of the SR platforms is dual stack (meaning it supports routing IPv4 and IPv6 traffic in parallel) and able to handle full BGP table.

articleTitle: Optimization of the iterative decoding algorithms for irregular block codes
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the performances of iterative decoders for linear block codes. In particular, we consider two modifications of the gradient-descent bit flipping (GDBF) algorithm with momentum, where multiple component decoders with different momentum values are concatenated to improve the decoder performance. The learning parameters of the component decoders are obtained by using a Genetic algorithm based on the database of the uncorrectable error patterns of the previous decoder. We present three optimization strategies and provide a comparison with the state-of-the-art decoders. The numerical results are presented on short Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes and the channel with additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN).

articleTitle: Enhanced IDS detection: Merging Statistical Analysis with Shapley Value Techniques
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have been instructed to protect networks and detect malicious traffic. Modern IDSs increasingly use Artificial Intelligence, but the complexity of network traffic complicates attack detection. This work introduces a framework that reduces dataset features using statistical tools and applies the Shapley Value from game theory to improve understanding of attack behaviours. The approach standardizes dataset analysis and ensures reproducibility in Machine Learning experiments, addressing a key challenge in AI-driven IDS research.

articleTitle: Distributed Simulation Framework for Assesing Multipath Transport Protocols
abstract: Several simulation frameworks have been developed to evaluate multipath transport protocols. However, only a few enable interaction with protocols implemented on real hardware, such as FPGA platforms. This paper proposes a Distributed Simulation Framework (DSF) that features two distinct software components, which can run on separate platforms: the Hybrid User Terminal (HUT) and the Device. The HUT generates data, configures devices, and provides insights into system behavior during simulations. In contrast, the Device is designed to operate on real hardware, such as FPGA boards. To demonstrate the potential of the DSF, the HUT was run on a PC-based machine, and the Device was run on a Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC ZCU111 Evaluation Kit. The results showed that the DSF delivers a wide range of data that can be used to evaluate multipath transport protocols effectively.

articleTitle: Unit Test Generation Multi-Agent AI System for Enhancing Software Documentation and Code Coverage
abstract: Software development necessitates a robust testing plan though test development can be laborious and nonappealing task. We explore the utilization of the application artificial intelligence agents for generating and executing unit tests, enhancing the “Mostly Basic Python Problems” dataset. We employ behavior-driven development within a three-agent system to generate user stories and unit tests. Empirical results indicate improvements in branch coverage, illustrating the effective utilization of large language models in software testing and development processes.

articleTitle: Comparison of Antennas Operating at 2.4 GHz for Microwave Hyperthermia Treatment of Breast Cancer
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the most common cancers affecting women globally. While traditional treatment methods often involve chemotherapy and radiation therapy, microwave hyperthermia presents a promising complementary approach by enhancing the effectiveness of these modalities. This study investigates three antenna designs operating at 2.4 GHz, applied to four-layer breast models with varying sizes and tumor locations. The results from these three unitary excited antennas demonstrate that the tumor can reach temperatures of 42 °C within 30 seconds to 4 minutes, while the temperature of the highly conductive skin tissue varies between 43 °C and 60 °C. These findings suggest that the choice of antenna is critical not only for effective target heating but also for preserving healthy tissue. Additionally, a trade-off was observed between treatment time and the safety of surrounding healthy tissue in a fixed antenna input power study.

articleTitle: Realizacija sigurnog mašinskog učenja u oblaku korišćenjem homomorfne enkripcije
abstract: Cilj ovog rada je da se reši problem privatnosti podataka prilikom obrade u oblaku, korišćenjem homomorfne enkripcije, preciznije, upotrebom CKKS šeme enkripcije. Za demonstraciju izabrano je da se osetljivi podaci koriste za obučavanje i ocenjivanje modela logističke regresije, na serveru u oblaku. Glavni fokus je poređenje performansi prilikom obrade plaintext i ciphertext podataka. Upotreba homomorfne enkripcije dovodi do obrade koja je sporija od 1000 do 6500 puta.

articleTitle: Detecting ugly and derogatory words in Serbian language using a web browser extension
abstract: In natural language processing, data acquisition and preprocessing techniques are significant for experiments involving training models on cleaned data. This paper describes the formation of a dataset of ugly and derogatory words in the Serbian language and the development of a web extension to analyze texts in which such words appear and then their censoring. Developing such an add-on is essential in creating a safer and healthier digital environment for young users who are just developing their Internet habits and adults who want to avoid unwanted content. It is crucial to point out that there are few software tools for natural languages with limited resources, such as the Serbian language. This software could analyze the frequency of certain foul words on different sites, which would contribute to a better understanding of the impact of such language on users.

articleTitle: Refining Directed Graphs for Spectral Analysis through Strategic Topological Modifications
abstract: In graph signal processing, the absence of a well-defined graph Fourier transform complicates spectral analysis on directed graphs. To address this, we propose a technique that subtly modifies the graph’s topology, making minimal changes to facilitate spectral analysis.Our approach starts by adding edges to eliminate sources and sinks, followed by identifying connections that impede the non-singularity and diagonalizability of the adjacency matrix. We then make minor edge weight adjustments to achieve diagonalizability, ensuring efficient spectral analysis of graph signals defined on directed graph.

articleTitle: A Multi-Resources Load-Balancing Policy in SDN
abstract: In this paper we introduce a Multi-Resource LoadBalancing policy that exploits the programmability of SDN to intelligently distribute the users’ traffic across a cluster of web servers based on four key metrics of the web servers: CPU, Memory, Bandwidth utilization, and Response Time. We evaluated and demonstrated how the proposal outperform not only naive load-balancing strategies, like Random and Round Robin, but also more informed and sophisticated ones.

articleTitle: DC Bias Line Design for Supply-Modulated Power Amplifiers
abstract: In this study, the design characteristics of the DC bias lines are aimed at constructing by minimizing the deteriorating effects on linearity for supply-modulated power amplifiers. The supply modulation phenomenon is carried out to enhance the back-off efficiency of the power amplifiers. In this paper, the design and implementation details of DC bias lines are introduced. Then, to evaluate the performance, linear and electromagnetic simulations are compared using the S-parameters.

articleTitle: A Hybrid (FSO-RF) System Model with Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Early Warning of Natural Disasters: Conceptual Approach
abstract: Hybrid systems integrating Free-Space Optics (FSO) and Radio Frequency (RF) technologies can provide robust early warning capabilities for natural disasters. By combining the advantages of both FSO and RF, such systems offer redundancy, reliability, and increased coverage, ensuring timely alerts and communication in the event of disasters. Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces can indeed be utilized to dynamically switch between RF and FSO communication modes, offering a flexible and efficient approach to adapt to changing environmental conditions. However, the deployment of Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) in hybrid RF/FSO systems is still relatively limited and requires further investigations to fully understand and optimize their integration. In this paper, the concept of integrating a Liquid Crystal IRS (LC-IRS) into a hybrid FSO/RF system for early warning and identification of natural disasters is discussed. The concept relies on sending data between a set of sensor nodes when a disaster does not exist and reflecting it back to a controlling base station when a natural disaster exists. The switching between these paths is controlled by the IRS. The IRS also works to control switching between the FSO and RF communication links based on the existing weather conditions. The variation in the reflection angle of the LC-IRS can be controlled by an external field as indicated in this paper. The suggested model in this paper provides a conceptual approach for the deployment of IRS in early warning systems.

articleTitle: Synchronization and Thermal Optimization of a Two-Channel SEPIC Converter System
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study of the thermal management and synchronization of a two-channel single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) system designed to power warning light bulbs in level-crossing signalling devices. The system replaces an older model, offering enhanced electrical performance and more compact dimensions. Thermal optimization is achieved by comparing heat dissipation strategies, including attaching heat sinks to the package top versus the PCB bottom. The analysis shows significant improvements in thermal management with bottom cooling. Additionally, synchronization techniques, particularly through external clocking, are employed to ensure stable operation and mitigate interference between converters. Experimental results validate both the thermal models and synchronization approach, showcasing reduced noise, and reliable converter performance.

articleTitle: Model-Based FPGA AI Accelerator Design Using Vitis AI with In-Depth Performance and Energy Efficiency Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a model-based design of AI accelerator following the Vitis TRD flow, implemented on the AMD Kria KV260 Vision AI Starter Kit. The ResNet-18 model, developed in PyTorch, was quantized, compiled with Vitis AI, and deployed to the FPGA via PYNQ. We deeply analyzed different DPU configurations and frequencies, focusing on resource utilization, power, FPS, and energy efficiency. Results show that resource utilization remains constant across frequencies, but lower frequencies increase energy consumption. For optimal performance and energy efficiency, high-MAC DPU configurations should be used at higher frequencies. To our knowledge, no prior research has fully detailed the Vitis TRD flow within Vitis AI. Most rely on Vivado TRD, which requires PetaLinux. This work offers a comprehensive guide for deploying AI models on FPGAs using Ubuntu, eliminating the need for PetaLinux expertise.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Analysis of a PWM DAC with a First-Order Passive RC Filter
abstract: This paper presents an exact analysis of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) utilizing a first-order RC filter. Through exact theoretical analysis in time domain, the study evaluates how the selected filter components impact mean value and ripple of the output voltage and settling time of the converter, which are the crucial factors for the estimation of accuracy and speed of conversion.

articleTitle: Fast Compressed Sensing Beam Training in RIS-assisted MISO Systems
abstract: This paper is dedicated to the problem of Beam Training (BT) in Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)assisted systems. There is a lack of BT solutions for the case when both the RIS and the user positions are unknown. Furthermore, the most popular solution (hierarchical search) requires frequent feedback from the user. We propose a joint BS and RIS scanning, which provides stable Compressed Sensing (CS) Channel Acquisition (CA) independent from RIS and user angular positions. Simulation results show that proposed method, while using feedback only once, is competitive with the hierarchical scheme. Another experiment ensures reduced dependence on initialization: optimized measurements provide up to 3 times less deviation of successful recovery probability in comparison with random measurements (10% and 30% respectively).

articleTitle: CPW-fed fractal slot antenna for microwave biosensing applications
abstract: A primary focus in biosensing applications has been on using microwave signals for wirelessly sensing life activities, capturing the interest of experts in radar systems and healthcare. Innovations like embedded DSP, FMCW radar, and deep learning algorithms have emerged from this research, extending applications to the Internet of Things (IoT), occupancy sensing, and security authentication. Future research emphasizes the need for cost-effective solutions, particularly in antenna design, which should be simple, compact, wideband, and easy to manufacture.The antennas used in these applications should be easy to manufacture on a PCB, and since they involve sensitive electronics, the front-to-back ratio on radiation pattern must be below 20 dB. This paper proposes a wideband antenna with a reflector that meets these criteria. Given its use in radars for biosensing applications, it is essential that the mutual coupling between two antennas placed side by side is less than -25 dB. Measurements of this antenna's parameters were conducted at a frequency of 2.4 GHz, which is the range for its intended use.

articleTitle: CUDA Calculation of Shannon Entropy for a Sliding Window System
abstract: Entropy algorithms are crucial in fields where assessing randomness, uncertainty, or complexity is vital. As datasets grow, efficient entropy calculations become important. This work explores the parallelization of Shannon entropy calculations, using GPU acceleration through CUDA for sliding window systems. By leveraging GPUs’ parallel architecture, the approach achieves up to 15x speedup for large datasets. However, smaller datasets show limited improvements due to overhead, underscoring the need for optimization to harness GPU acceleration’s potential.

articleTitle: Perturbation on Feature Coalition: Towards Interpretable Deep Neural Networks
abstract: The inherent "black box" nature of deep neural networks (DNNs) compromises their transparency and reliability. Recently, explainable AI (XAI) has garnered increasing attention from researchers. Several perturbation-based interpretations have emerged. However, these methods often fail to adequately consider feature dependencies. To solve this problem, we introduce a perturbation-based interpretation guided by feature coalitions, which leverages deep information of network to extract correlated features. Then, we proposed a carefully-designed consistency loss to guide network interpretation. Both quantitative and qualitative experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Code is available at github.com/Teriri1999/Perturebation-on-Feature-Coalition.

articleTitle: MicroPython Testbed for Federated Learning Algorithms
abstract: The original Python Testbed for Federated Learning Algorithms (PTB-FLA) is a light FL framework, which provides generic centralized and decentralized federated learning algorithms, but has the limitation that all the application instances can run only on a single PC. This paper presents the MicroPyton Testbed for Federated Learning Algorithms (MPT-FLA), the new framework that overcomes this limitation such that individual application instances may run on different network nodes like PCs and IoTs, primarily in edge systems. The new framework was validated and evaluated on a wireless LAN of PCs and RPi Pico W boards and wired LAN of PCs, respectively, by using application examples originally developed for the predecessor framework.

articleTitle: Innovative Approach to Accelerating Laravel Backend Generation from Vue.js Components Using Axios, Artificial Intelligence and Artisan Commands
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative system for automatically creating backend resources in a Laravel environment. Web application development often requires significant time and resources due to manual backend setup after creating frontend components. Here, we present a method that optimizes web application development by automating the creation of Laravel backend resources directly from Vue.js components using Axios, Artisan commands, and artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed method allows automatic generation of models, migrations, and controllers on the backend immediately after creating a Vue.js component on the frontend. This reduces development time and human error, making the process more efficient and consistent. The paper details the implementation of this method, its impact on development efficiency, and analysis results compared to traditional web development methods. Based on the research results, it was concluded that applying this method reduces initial development time by 33.96% in Laravel applications which is a scientific contribution to this paper.

articleTitle: The Usage of Electroimpedance Tomography along with Artificial Intelligence in Application Development in the field of Medicine
abstract: This study investigates the integration of Electroimpedance Tomography (EIT) with Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) for enhanced object detection and imaging in medical and robotics applications. The study encompasses data collection, processing, and image construction, along with algorithms for evaluation and classification. The validity of the system is done by assessing algorithm accuracy by comparing the system results with the physical results. The study also identifies the areas for future improvement such as measurement complexity and data collection automation, underscoring EIT's potential for advancing diagnostics.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation for Local Energy Communities: Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Local Energy Communities (LECs) are a key element of the transition to a low-carbon economy, as they enable citizens, businesses, and public entities to produce, consume, and share renewable energy. To operate and integrate effectively into the energy system, LECs need to digitalize and semantically interoperate their data. However, LECs encounter several obstacles to achieving full digitalization, such as the lack of common standards and vocabularies, the diversity of data sources and formats, the privacy and security issues, and the need for user-friendly and scalable solutions. Moreover, LECs face challenges in collecting and analysing the data necessary to model the behaviour of building occupants, energy flexible resources, distributed generation, and grid conditions, which are essential for improving the design and operation of LECs in a variety of real-world settings and increase community engagement. In this paper, these challenges have been analysed and recommendations have been provided, based on the experience gained through OMEGA-X project. By developing a multi vector energy data space and innovative data-driven services, OMEGA-X enables local energy communities to maximize renewable energy use, reduce costs, contribute to decarbonization and achieve collective self-consumption. Two project’s pilot sites, a residential energy community in Portugal and a commercial energy community in Serbia, have been presented to demonstrate the potential of data-driven platforms to optimize energy operations, engage citizens, and foster sustainable energy markets.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model for Generating Time Variant Gamma-Shadowed Ricean Fading Samples
abstract: When in the mobile radio channel there are simultaneous variations of the EM field due to multipath propagation and the shadowing effect, then the fluctuations of the composite signal envelope can be described using the Gamma shadowed Ricean distribution. For a precise analysis of the transmission of information through the radio channel, it is necessary to have a simulation model that takes into account the second order characteristics of this process. In this paper, we provide an approach for generating random process whose instantaneous values have the so-called Gamma-shadowed Ricean distribution. We present the time forms of the generated process, probability density function and autocovariance functions, and draw appropriate conclusions regarding the aforementioned characteristics.

articleTitle: CNN Vulnerability On Untargeted Adversarial Attacks
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are widely used in various AI-driven industries, including healthcare, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity, due to their high accuracy in image classification. However, these models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where small, imperceptible perturbations in input data can cause incorrect predictions. This study evaluates the impact of five adversarial attacks: Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Iterative FGSM (IFGSM), Momentum Iterative FGSM (MIFGSM), Deepfool, and OnePixel Attack on the accuracy of a CNN trained on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Each attack is analyzed for its unique influence on model performance, revealing significant accuracy drops under adversarial conditions. The results are analyzed and illustrate the potential security risks of adversarial attacks, underscoring the need for robust defenses in CNN based systems.

articleTitle: Case study of performance degradation on the Proxmox related to native host
abstract: This paper presents the file system performance comparison of native operating system and Proxmox hypervisor-based virtualization compared. Paper includes Centos in the role of the native/guest operating system, and Filebench as software for benchmarking. The tests performed on a native operating system, and on the same operating system in Proxmox virtual environment for one, two, three and four virtual machines. We set up a model of native and virtual environment. Model predicts the native operating system is remarkable faster than the virtual operating system. This paper confirms the model prediction, as solid file system performance drops due to virtualization.

articleTitle: Utilizing the Kokkos Framework for Scalable Application Parallelization
abstract: New, efficient parallel paradigms and models have been one of the main focuses of the research community in the domain of high-performance computing and multiprocessing systems. It is especially emphasized with the rise of many-core processors, such as graphics processing units. The development of parallel applications for different multi-core and many-core architectures becomes even harder, as it is usually needed to maintain different codebases. In this paper, we evaluate Kokkos, a new high-level parallel programming model and framework aimed at developing portable parallel programs for different architectures. We evaluated it using five different benchmark applications on the CPU and compared the results with OpenMP counterparts. The results and experiences are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Computer Vision on Edge: Using Edge Impulse and Deep Learning Models on Raspberry Pi
abstract: Some of the applications in the field of machine learning and computer vision may require a higher level of privacy and security, better cost efficiency, offline operation, and greater scalability and efficiency. This can be ensured by building machine learning and computer vision on edge devices. This paper presents solutions in the field of computer vision using deep learning models implemented in Edge Impulse and then deployed for use on the Raspberry Pi. Deep neural network models were used, YOLO (You Only Look Once), SSD (Single Shot MultiBox Detector), MobileNet, and EfficientDet.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Hotel Reviews: Applying Data Science for Enhanced Review Integrity
abstract: As the hotel industry increasingly relies on online reviews to attract and retain customers, distinguishing between genuine and fraudulent feedback has become critical. This paper presents a methodology for anomaly detection in hotel reviews by employing advanced exploratory data analysis (EDA). Key aspects of our analysis include evaluating sentiment and review similarity, uncovering unusual behavioral patterns, and identifying patterns in temporal posting trends and distributions. Time series analysis helps to recognize unusual spikes and shifts in user review activity. Additionally, we address issues such as misleading titles and ratings by tracing correlations among crucial review elements. This methodology provides actionable insights and recommendations for improving review filtering processes and addressing fraudulent content, offering a comprehensive analysis of online review patterns without relying on predictive modeling.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Vendor-Neutral Network Management Strategies
abstract: The ongoing advancement of computer networks toward efficient configuration of numerous devices has been driven by innovations in management and control technologies. Considering the limitations of the Command Line Interface (CLI) and Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) developed the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF). This protocol provides cross-vendor and interoperable solution for manipulating configuration states and leverages the Yet Another Next Generation (YANG) data models to describe network elements. This paper proposes an educational analysis of the capabilities for device configuration via the NETCONF protocol and YANG data models. The scope of the analysis is to illustrate the flexibility of the NETCONF protocol and the range of network features addressed by vendor-neutral models such as OpenConfig and IETF YANG models within contemporary networking environment.

articleTitle: AI in Software Testing: Revolutionizing Quality Assurance
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is an area of tremendous potential, especially in the software testing domain, where it has changed the dynamics of the process, storms in efficiency, accuracy, and flexibility in a given SDLC. This paper presents findings from recent investigations of AI in the testing and quality assurance focusing on its transformational potential. Particular attention is paid to such issues as automation of testing processes through AI, testing process enhancement, and possible changes in software engineering due to AI implementation. In this paper, various research perspectives have been integrated to reveal the effectiveness of AI in enhancing the perceived quality assurance processes, improving product quality, and adopting principles of agile methodology in today's software development.

articleTitle: Speeding up Dense Optical Flow Estimation with CUDA
abstract: Optical flow is the perceived movement of a pixel within the video. It is inherently helpful for motion tracking and may also be used as a preprocessing for other computer vision algorithms or machine learning. Algorithmic optical flow estimation is slow and resource-intensive, but real-time performance can be achieved by using GPUs. This paper discusses implementing and optimizing a pyramidal Lucas-Kanade optical flow algorithm in CUDA.

articleTitle: Eksperimentalna analiza promenljivosti elektromagnetskog zračenja koje potiče od 5G bazne stanice
abstract: Interesovanje ljudi za izloženost elektromagnetskom zračenju koje potiče od baznih stanica je sve veće, pa se javlja potreba za objektivnom analizom. U ovom radu sprovedena je eksperimentalna analiza promenljivosti elektromagnetskog zračenja na jednoj mernoj poziciji u blizini 5G bazne stanice (5G BS). Merenje je sprovedeno za različite slučajeve opterećenja 5G BS – kada ne postoji prenos podataka sa 5G BS, kada je realizovan prenos podataka sa manjim protokom, kao i prenos sa većim protokom. Utvrđeno je da je srednja vrednost intenziteta električnog polja kada je realizovan prenos podataka sa većim protokom porasla gotovo 7 puta u odnosu na slučaj kada nema prenosa podataka sa 5G BS. Pored toga, određena je merna nesigurnost vezana za intervale usrednjavanja rezultata merenja od 15s, 30s, 1min i 6min, i pokazano je da se ona očekivano smanjuje sa povećanjem intervala usrednjavanja. Za interval usrednjavanja od 6min, merna nesigurnost je manja od 8%.

articleTitle: An architecture for Parzen-based multivariate probability density estimation
abstract: This paper proposes an architecture for multivariate probability density estimation using the Parzen window approach. As a non-parametric method, the Parzen approach provides reliable density estimates when sufficient data is available. It does not require prior information about the data, making it practical for real-world applications. The proposed solution eliminates the need for sorting operations, which are challenging to implement in hardware. Simulations conducted using PSpice software (OrCad version 22.1) demonstrate that the required processing time is less than 500 ns, underscoring the method's potential for fast and efficient probability density estimation.

articleTitle: Enhancing BLE-based positioning system performance with proximity sensors
abstract: Nowadays, a growing demand for LBS (Location Based Services) is being observed, which leads to the rapid development of new indoor location systems and the constant search for ways to improve positioning accuracy. Most popular localization systems, Wi-Fi and BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) based, suffer from the errors caused by the multipath propagation and attenuation of the radio waves. In the paper, a novel approach for the positioning accuracy improvement is presented. It utilizes the multi-zone infrared proximity sensor and its ability to measure the distance to the person and the possibility to estimate the angle at which the person is standing relative to the sensor.

articleTitle: Analysis of Security Mechanisms Used in ETL Tools
abstract: This paper analyses current best practices for using security mechanisms in extract, transform, and load (ETL) tools. The results of the analysis are visually represented in a form of an optimal security model used in these tools at the moment. In order to test the recommended model, it was implemented in a selected open source ETL tool. At the end, advantages and disadvantages of the recommended model are enlisted and directions for further improvement of the model are given.

articleTitle: RIS-Aided Uplink NOMA in the Presence of CCI
abstract: This paper investigates the co-channel interference (CCI) effects on the uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) users. The investigation considers that two NOMA users communicate with the base station (BS). The NOMA user close to the BS has a line of sight with the BS, while the far user only communicates with the BS via passive and absorptive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The investigation also considers that BS is under the effect of the randomly deployed CCI and interfere the received signal from the NOMA users. Performance of the aforementioned system is measured by means of the outage probability performance metric. Analytical derivations are verified by means of the Monte Carlo-based computer simulations. The results indicate that increasing the number of RIS elements degrades the outage performance for the near user but enhances it for the far user. Furthermore, the findings reveal that CCI causes minor loss in coding gain for NOMA users when the RIS has a small number of elements. However, this negative impact of CCI diminishes as the number of RIS elements increases.

articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Method for Air Quality Index Prediction with Diverse Sensor Quality Types
abstract: Air pollution critically affects public health, requiring accurate spatial and temporal air quality predictions. This study predicts the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Delhi, India, using high-cost and simulated low-cost sensors in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Temporal prediction utilizes Support Vector Regression (SVR), while spatial prediction uses a Deep Learning Neural Network (DLNN). The findings represent low-cost sensors as a cost-effective alternative for air quality monitoring and accurate AQI predictions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wireless Communication Technologies for use in Maritime IoT
abstract: Maritime IoT (Internet of Things) systems depend on robust communication techniques to ensure seamless data exchange and connectivity at sea. Effective design needs to consider coverage, data transfer rates, power consumption, and application-specific needs, along with redundancy for enhanced reliability. This paper analyzes key wireless communication technologies for maritime IoT, including their pros and cons. This analysis aims to guide engineers in a selection of adequate communication technologies for effective maritime IoT implementations.

articleTitle: Infrastructure for distributed PV systems monitoring and management using SCADA
abstract: Different types and different size photovoltaic (PV) systems are in use. Assuming that these systems are equipped with some of the devices: phasor measurement units (PMUs), internet of things (IoT) devices, intelligent electronic devices (IED) and that they are properly connected to the control center, or that inverters in the PV systems contain network interface cards (NIC-s) which are connected to the control center through network, a solution for infrastructure of the monitoring and management (M&M) system is proposed. The main parts of the system are cloud infrastructure on which supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system is implemented, network that connects all parts of cloud together and enables connections to the distributed devices at PV sites and distributed devices as well as inverters.

articleTitle: Potential Counteractions to Duty Cycle-Compliant Jamming in LoRa Networks
abstract: The LoRa protocol is designed for long-range communication with minimal energy consumption, ideal for IoT deployments over large distances. LoRa networks use unlicensed bands, making them vulnerable to jamming attacks. Ensuring security is crucial, especially in Massive IoT (M-IoT) scenarios. This work discusses a selective jamming attack that degrades communication in LoRaWAN deployments and proposes a countermeasure integrating attack mitigation and intrusion detection to address the issue.

articleTitle: Loop Unrolling Impact on CUDA Matrix Multiplication Operations
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of loop unrolling on CUDA matrix multiplication operations’ performance across NVIDIA GPUs. We benchmarked both basic and unrolled kernels with varying unroll factors (2, 4, 8, and 16) and CUDA block sizes (8, 16, and 32) on matrices ranging from 128 × 128 to 4096 × 4096. Using two GPUs, the GeForce RTX 4060 and GTX TITAN X, we analyze how unrolling factors impact execution time. Our findings indicate that loop unrolling, particularly with factors of 8 and 16 and a block size of 32, yields significant performance gains on larger matrices. These results confirm loop unrolling as an effective optimization technique for CUDA matrix operations, providing insights for developers to enhance computational efficiency across different GPU architectures.

articleTitle: Information system for heart rate monitoring of cardiovascular patients
abstract: Modern IoT devices used for remote health monitoring use basic parameters such as heart rate, skin temperature and oxygen saturation. Maximum heart rate is an important parameter used for calculating heart rate zones that is helpful in diagnosis and prevention of cardiovascular diseases. This paper presents an information system that contains an IoT subsystem for heart rate measurement, and a web-server subsystem for monitoring by doctors that includes heart rate zone monitoring.

articleTitle: Ispitivanje performansi prototipa industrijskog CT skenera
abstract: U radu su predstavljeni rezultati ispitivanja performansi prototipa CT skenera namenjenog nedestruktivnom testiranju industrijskih komponenti. Sprovedena je kontrola kvaliteta tomografskih slika namenski izrađenog fantoma i izabranih proizvodnih artikala. Rezultati ispitivanja ukazali su na potrebu korekcije projekcija dobijenih akvizicijom, zbog neporavnatosti ose rotacije platforme skenera sa centrom prijemnika slike. Po izvršenoj korekciji, verifikovana je mogućnost prilagođenja kondicija skenera osobinama testiranih objekata, sa stanovišta uočljivosti strukturnih detalja na rekonstruisanim slikama.

articleTitle: Methodology for Research and Determination of Complex Cyber Attacks in Corporate Networks
abstract: Cybersecurity professionals are valuable assets nowadays, considering the constantly emerging obscure security threats. However, the volume of security incidents in the modern corporate networks often surpasses the capacity of the teams managing the security stack, leading to incident fatigue within organizations. In this paper, we propose a methodology that leverages context-aware predictions based on historical incident data to ease the decision making process for the security teams. Using Learning Vector Quantization neural networks, our approach helps to efficiently differentiate between false positive and true positive incidents, providing with actionable insights, and reducing the time spent on irrelevant alerts.

articleTitle: Edge-Based Anomaly Detection: Enhancing Performance and Sustainability of Cyber-Attack Detection in Smart Water Distribution Systems
abstract: Recent advancements in cyber-physical systems have significantly increased the vulnerability of water distribution systems to cyber attacks, necessitating robust detection mechanisms. This study evaluates a decentralized detection model, leveraging edge computing to enhance the timeliness and efficiency of anomaly detection while minimizing energy consumption and carbon emissions. Despite a slight 0.4% decrease in overall performance compared to centralized systems, the decentralized model showed a 0.015% improvement in the mean time to detection, outperforming both the centralized benchmark and existing literature values. The reduction of energy consumption and emissions during training are estimated with approximately 75%, while in inference the estimate of emission reductions spans two orders of magnitude. Moreover, we demonstrate a significant advancement in attack localization, successfully assigning detected anomalies to three specific edge areas of the network. Our approach not only addresses the immediate challenges of cybersecurity in water distribution systems but also contributes to the broader goal of sustainable and resilient infrastructure.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Breast Region in Magnetic Resonance Images - Evaluation of Template-Based Approach
abstract: Automatic detection of suspicious lesions in breast MRI images is hindered by the presence of internal organs of similar intensities in post-contrast MRI images. In this study we applied a template-based algorithm to mask internal organs, efficiently removing anatomical structures outside the region of interest. In the absence of manual annotations of the region of interest, quantitative and qualitative analysis revealed that the proposed approach achieved satisfactory results in identification of internal organs in 99.07% subjects. After successful masking of internal organs, breast and axillary fossae region segmentation is efficiently performed using clustering and morphological operations.

articleTitle: RIS Deployment Evaluation with Easy-to-Use Simulator
abstract: The evaluation of new technologies in networks requires the use of reliable simulation tools. As the complexity of the network increases, so does the complexity of the simulation tool. This paper presents an easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) for the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) capable Vienna 5G System-Level Simulator developed within the scope of the European Meta Wireless project. The simulation tool evaluates the performance gains achieved by deploying RIS in an urban scenario with blocked line of sight (LOS) connections. This paper shows that the network throughput can be enhanced through the deployment of RISs that increase the received power at user equipment in low-coverage areas reducing the outage from 61% outage to 19%.

articleTitle: A 24GHz heterodyne CMOS receiver in 65nm technology
abstract: A 24GHz CMOS RF receiver for short range applications is developed in this paper. This paper presents the design of a heterodyne receiver and the results achieved. Heterodyne receivers are advantageous in eliminating DC offset problems, suppressing flicker noise and 2nd order non-linearity, due to the two-step down-conversion topology. The proposed RF IC includes a low-noise amplifier (LNA), two down-conversion mixers (one for lowering the working frequency to the first intermediate frequency (IF1) range (4.4GHz - 5.2GHz), and the other for lowering to the baseband frequency (IF2) range ( - 20kHz)), and two amplifiers for each IF for additional power gain. The main goal of achieving a high conversion gain and low noise are met, with results showing a conversion gain of 77dB (voltage gain of 98dB) and a noise figure of 6.39dB with a power consumption of 62.5mW.

articleTitle: Large Language Model for Financial Insights: Building a Digest to Simplify Research Activities
abstract: The world is drowning in various types of data. Every day, researchers and professionals are bombarded with a torrent of news, reports, and academic papers – far too much for anyone to process manually. This information overload makes it incredibly challenging to stay ahead of the curve and identify emerging trends in finance. Finance is the field of study that we are going to focus on in this article.This research introduces a solution: AI Digest, an automated service powered by Google's Gemini large language model (LLM). We demonstrate how AI Digest can effortlessly walk through this large flow of articles and scientific papers, extracting key insights and trends from vast quantities of financial text. Imagine if you have a tireless research assistant who can summarize hundreds of articles, pinpoint emerging patterns, and present it all in a concise, digestible report. That's precisely what AI Digest aims to achieve.Our study describes the development and architecture of AI Digest, showcasing its ability to summarize large amounts of text and identify valuable insights. We highlight the advantages of using LLMs for analysis articles, and how LLM can not only save significant time but also uncover hidden trends. Furthermore, we provide a glimpse into the future of modern LLM and NLP (Natural language processing) models, and how they are slowly integrating in our daily routine.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Modeling Communication in SoCs for the Shift-Left Paradigm using IEEE 1666 SystemC
abstract: In the realm of system level design and verification of complex communication systems, several modeling and simulation tools play a crucial role. Among which, Real Number Modeling is of prime importance. In the process of complex modeling, the shift-left paradigm allows testing and validation in an earlier phase and leads to a higher quality system, with reduced cost and shorter development cycles. Real Number Modeling is capable of handling mixed-signal simulations with both digital and analog elements in the same discrete event environment. This paper deals with identifying modeling paradigms in IEEE 1666 (SystemC), with speed as the prime consideration.The investigation covers three primary aspects – the first being a comprehensive comparison of speed performance in models, ranging from complex to simple executed in SystemC DE (Discrete Event), SystemC TDF (Timed Data Flow) and both (TDF+DE). The analysis begins with a complex scenario such as that of a Receiver and further breaks down to simpler ones such as a Low Noise Amplifier. In both cases a mixed model (TDF+DE) is observed to be the fastest. The second aspect deals with analysing the behaviour of SystemC DE and TDF with M number of connected modules in chain and parallel setups. TDF approach is seen to have a performance advantage here, provided the modules are connected to a single source. The third aspect details on factors experimented to save computation time while modeling a system. Among which, the use of datatype converters and number of modules in a cluster are the evaluated elements. Results discussed in the paper show that there are still undiscovered, yet considerable opportunities for improvement in this domain.

articleTitle: Examination of the Resolution Parameter in an Image Denoising Algorithm Based on Fractional Diffusion
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of resolution parameter values on image denoising performances. A fractional anisotropic diffusion partial differential equation, solved in the Fourier domain, is employed as the denoising algorithm. The algorithm is varied based on resolution in the Fourier domain resulting in higher time steps and increased efficiency. Quality of the proposed variation is further examined using SNR, PSNR, and MSSSIM measures and the obtained results are discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of heart rate monitoring accuracy of smart wearable technology devices
abstract: Smart wearable devices often contain heart rate monitoring capabilities. This paper presents an experimental study that compares the accuracy of smart watches (Xiaomi Amazfit Bip 3 and GEEKIN X10) to microcontroller-based systems that use raw sensors (HW-827 and MAX30102). The achieved results indicate that the accuracy of raw sensors is lower compared to smart watches and that the level of inaccuracy depends on the level of physical activity of the test subjects.

articleTitle: Multi-Connectivity Framework Based on Open-Source 5G Network Core
abstract: The 5th generation of mobile networks (5G) offers significant advantages and numerous use cases for industries and customers providing more reliable and high speed connections to millions of devices. Currently there are many open source implementations of architectures based on Software Defined Networking (SDN). In this paper, we focus on Free5gc implementation of 5G core network and we provide a scalable test environment using UERANSIM project for Radio Access Network (RAN) and User Equipment (UE) network components. We create an example scenario with one free5gc 5G network core, one gNB component and 2 UE devices, with an external client connected to both UE devices. We create an example flow where external client, through TCP connections to UE devices, access the Internet. Also, we provide a resource analysis that shows balanced resource utilization, and identify potential directions for further research.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer Based Adaptive Beamforming for GNSS Bands
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are the most used navigation method nowadays. However, GNSS signals are often jammed on purpose. Therefore, it became necessary to eliminate these jammer signals to obtain navigation data. In this study, a vision transformer based adaptive beamforming method (ViT-BF) is presented to suppress jammer signals. As the difference from the previously studied ViT based beamforming approaches, the model is built with autocorrelation matrix as input and beamforming weights as output, which provides a blind beamforming method. ViT-BF approach is compared with a previously proposed convolutional neural network based beamforming (CNN-BF) and noise subspace tracking (NST), which ViT-BF is resulted more successfully in terms of beam and null divergences in directions of signal arrivals and with a shorter response time.

articleTitle: Improvements in information security using the example of a web application for automatic class schedule generation
abstract: JavaScript is one of the programming languages used to create dynamic web applications. Due to its dynamic nature, it can often be a target for creating unwanted content on web pages. This paper presents the results of testing the Skedyul application, designed for automatic class schedule generation in schools. The study analyzes vulnerabilities of JavaScript as a scripting language and their impact on the security of web applications. JavaScript, being a key language for web programming, is frequently targeted in attacks due to its widespread use and inherent vulnerabilities. The paper identifies major types of JavaScript vulnerabilities, including XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) and CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery). Methods for protecting against these vulnerabilities are discussed, such as input sanitization, using secure libraries and frameworks, and regular software updates. The importance of security awareness and implementing best practices in web application development is emphasized to reduce the risk of attacks based on JavaScript vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Techniques for Generated Speech Detection
abstract: This work is aimed at investigating the possibility of generated speech detection using machine learning techniques. The study was conducted on the basis of open datasets (CFAD, FoR), as well as on the basis of personal dataset created by the model of DeepFake speech generation RVC-v2. The study proved that speech could be detected on all three datasets as well as on the combination of all three datasets at 16 kHz sampling rate.

articleTitle: Dual Band Substrate Integrated Waveguide Based MIMO Antenna With DGS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a 2-port dual-band SIW MIMO antenna for Ku-band (17.1–20.1 GHz), K and Ka band (23.1–27.5 GHz) applications. The proposed MIMO antenna is based on a cavity slot antenna based on a newly proposed DGS structure fed by a Y-junction power divider. The multimode high-order resonances are excited within the cavity resonator using four vias to obtain dual broadband performance. We optimize the DGS structure as a bandpass filter for unwanted frequency resonance and a radiating slot. The antenna achieves realized gains between 6 and 7.5 dBi for the Ku band and between 5 and 6 dBi for the mmWave band for the respective bands, with corresponding radiation efficiencies of > 85% and > 90%. Lastly, suitable values of both ECC and DG are achieved.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Algorithm to Compute Intermodulation Distortion of Arbitrary Signals in Frequency Domain
abstract: Intermodulation distortion (IMD) arises in all analogue circuitry, due to always-present nonlinearities. Although they may be very weak, due to near-far problem in wireless communications large level discrepancies are faced. IMD spectra may shade weak ones and turn e.g. a receiver blind and imply outage of communication. In MIMO transmitters, a problem called reverse intermodulation is faced, leading into wideband emission and signal integrity degradation. We present here an algorithm of low complexity that efficiently computes the intermodulation spectra in receivers and transmitters for NLTI (non-linear time invariant) systems. Thus, the only prerequisite we demand is memoryless behavior of system, which holds well for receivers and transmitters unless they are driven deeply into saturation. The algorithm is largely based on iFFT/FFT and Isserli’s theorem. It is capable of computing IM3, IM5 and IM7 effects. Further, it provides large insight into the compression mechanisms present in receivers and transmitters and how each IM order contributes to the overall spectrum. By that, we overcome the simple treatment of intermodulation with unmodulated two-tone test or the time consuming computation of intermodulation with modulated signals in time domain.

articleTitle: Entropy Analysis of Electrocardiograms for Cognitive Performance Evaluation
abstract: In recent times, we have witnessed a significant expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the development of machine learning algorithms for various applications. In this context, selecting relevant features is crucial. Cognitive load tests affect physiological signals such as electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This paper deals with an initial collecting of ECGs during cognitive effect examination using a low-cost system. The signals correspond to states before and after the volunteer performs a cognitive test. Besides heart rate variability, in this paper entropy analysis is performed. The obtained effects and possibilities of distinguishing between the states before and after the cognitive test are also considered.

articleTitle: Exploring the visual CAD capabilities of ChatGPT: An experimental study
abstract: Generative AI approaches such as ChatGPT are very popular and can be used for multiple purposes. This paper explores the possibility of using ChatGPT-4o for analysing visual information about 2D objects on provided images and returning annotated image results to the user. The achieved results indicate that ChatGPT can be used for the analysis of visual data and detect approximate values of desired parameters, however its generative capabilities are lacking and often unusable.

articleTitle: Atrial fibrillation detection using a hybrid 1D CNN-KNN architecture
abstract: Early detection of atrial fibrillation plays a crucial role in the timely prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. This paper proposes two different network architectures for automated atrial fibrillation detection. In the first architecture, a 1D CNN is used as a feature extractor and classifier. In the second hybrid architecture, a 1D CNN is used only as a feature extractor from ECG time series signals that supply a KNN with the most relevant features for further classification. Experimental results showed that the hybrid architecture achieved remarkable results and outperformed a 1D CNN.

articleTitle: Positioning in WLAN Networks Based on SVM Algorithms and Space Segmentation
abstract: Due to the widespread availability of WLAN networks, positioning techniques in these environments have become a subject of intense research. In this paper, a combination of Support Vector Classification (SVC) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) machine learning algorithms was used, along with space segmentation, to solve the problem of user localization in a WLAN network. The proposed technique was thoroughly tested in a real WLAN environment. The lowest mean positioning error was achieved when the space was divided into 6 subspaces, amounting to 7.69m.

articleTitle: File system performance comparison between Linux-based hypervisors ESXi and Proxmox
abstract: This paper presents the file system performance a comparison of Linux-based hypervisors (type-1). ESXi and Proxmox were selected representing the typical type-1 Linux-based hypervisors. Both hypervisors contain similar Linux-based architectures at first sight, but in the details, significant differences will appear. For our experiments, we have chosen Filebench as the benchmarking tool. Filebench is recognized for its great flexibility and adaptability. This benchmark allows the simulation of real server applications. Linux distribution CentOS 9, was employed as the guest operating system. Our tests operated with few virtual machines, simultaneously (one to four). This paper includes a math model of the Linux-based virtual environments (type-1), which is associated by a proper experiment in the form of a specific case study. We utilize the model to explain the experimental performance results.

articleTitle: Identifying Image Compression Methods Using Vision Transformers
abstract: Image compression uses various lossy methods, each creating different distortions. Understanding these distortions is key for optimizing image enhancement and steganography, as they affect quality and detectability. Detection of compression algorithms is essential especially when file extensions are altered. This study presents a method for identifying compression algorithms - JPEG, AVIF, HEIC, and WebP, using a fine-tuned vision transformer model. The model achieved 98% validation and 99% test accuracy and shows premising results.

articleTitle: Integrating DMA for Efficient 3D Audio Processing in Resource-Constrained DSP Systems
abstract: In the rapidly advancing digital landscape, immersive sound technologies have emerged as transformative elements in enhancing user experiences across various media platforms, including film, gaming, and music. This paper explores the complexity of 3D audio, focusing on complex processing and volumes of data that meet contemporary broadcasting standards and enhances user interaction. We propose the integration of DMA to offer quick data access that enables advanced audio applications to operate within limited resources.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Oscilloscope Devices for Research Laboratory Usage
abstract: In this paper, the STEMlab 125-14 device used as a portable oscilloscope is evaluated in comparison with Siglent dual channel SDS1052DL+ oscilloscope. Both oscilloscopes are tested according to EURAMET calibration guidelines using Time Electronics 5025E multifunction calibrator with its internal executable programs for oscilloscope calibration. The main purpose of this paper is to define the limitations of using the evaluated devices in the research laboratory with the main application in the field of optoelectronics.

articleTitle: Application of the Sionna Software for 5G/6G Physical Layer Simulations
abstract: The rapid advancement of wireless communication technologies demands sophisticated simulation software capable of accurately modeling and analyzing the physical layer of 5G (Fifth Generation). Advanced applications of the Sionna software provide a comprehensive platform for simulating complex link dynamics and performance metrics. This research focuses on the simulation analyses of 5G NR (New Radio) LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) codes and Multi-User MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing) techniques, demonstrating significant improvements in system performance and channel efficiency. The integration of ML (Machine Learning) methods is essential for advancing signal processing and decoding efficiency, particularly in next-generation networks. Simulated advanced neural demapping techniques highlight the need for innovative approaches to address the challenges posed by emerging technologies, including anticipated advancements in 6G (Sixth Generation).

articleTitle: Evaluating Azure Container, Backend, and Function as a Service
abstract: In this research paper, we investigate the performance of Container, Backend, and Function as a Service as various Microsoft cloud service models for specific computational and memory-bound use cases. The research method involves practical experiments to present insights into functionalities, advantages, and limitations. Our research shows that AKS performs the best compared to Web Apps and Azure Functions, reaching the highest throughput for a quick sort application.

articleTitle: A New Tanh-based Algorithm for Acoustic Feedback Cancellation
abstract: In this paper, a new tanh-based is proposed for the acoustic feedback cancellation in hearing aids. It uses the proportionate affine projection tanh algorithm, combined with a novel neural network-based stability detector. Our simulations and the 32-bit floating point implementation indicate that the proposed algorithm can be an attractive alternative to the considered competing AFC algorithms for incoming speech and music signals.

articleTitle: PolarFire FPGA Radiation Endurance Testing Platform
abstract: Radiation endurance testing is crucial for electronic components used in environments with high levels of ionizing radiation, such as aerospace, military, and certain medical applications. This paper presents a testing platform designed to evaluate the radiation tolerance of FPGAs, particularly focusing on a flash-based FPGA from Microchip’s PolarFire family. The system architecture integrates a device under test (DUT) and a tester FPGA on the same board, with supporting hardware to monitor and record radiation-induced errors. A simplified power topology was proposed to reduce complexity without compromising stability. Additionally, the platform supports high-speed data acquisition and real-time error analysis, offering a reliable solution for FPGA radiation testing.

articleTitle: Open-Source Software for Microwave Ablation Analysis
abstract: In this paper, we use a full 3D finite element method for microwave ablation simulation based on open-source software. A real large tumor taken from the database is used and two probes are used for treatment. The effects of using power control and changing the size and shape of the ablation with the same applied energy are shown.

articleTitle: High performance low pass harmonic rejection filter for microwave, mm wave radar/5G-6G applications
abstract: Nowadays as of highly congested radio spectrum there is considerable need for high quality filters. On one side filters help to keep spurious signals level in a system low and maintain their high performances, while on the other side - they prevent unwanted interference signals to propagate externally and degrade functionality of other surrounding communication systems ensuring electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). In this paper an interesting solution for high performances low pass harmonic filter is presented for application in portable radar system. The filter belongs to the class of waffle iron filters however it is with asymmetrical construction which gives better performances than commonly used symmetrical ones.

articleTitle: Tackling heavy-tailed noise in distributed estimation: Asymptotic performance and tradeoffs
abstract: We present an algorithm for distributed estimation of an unknown vector parameter θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup> ∈ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sup> in the presence of heavy-tailed observation and communication noises. Heavy-tailed noises frequently appear, e.g., in densely deployed Internet of Things (IoT) or wireless sensor network systems. The presented algorithm falls within the class of consensus+innovation estimators and combats the effect of the heavy-tailed noises by adding general nonlinearities in the consensus and innovations update parts. We present results on almost sure convergence and asymptotic normality of the estimator. In addition, we provide novel analytical studies that reveal interesting tradeoffs between the system noises and the underlying network topology.

articleTitle: Analysis of network attack classification success and extraction of the most important features
abstract: The rapid increase in the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has raised security concerns due to their simplistic architectures. Attacks on these devices can compromise user privacy and disrupt critical infrastructure. This paper focuses on selecting key features from the UNB CIC IOT 2023 dataset to improve network attack classification success using machine learning algorithms and evaluates the effectiveness of existing network monitoring tools in detecting these features. The XGBoost algorithm achieved the highest F1 score of approximately 0.93.

articleTitle: Comparison of Ensemble Methods for Sentiment Analysis in Serbian Language
abstract: Sentiment analysis plays a significant role in natural language processing (NLP). This paper compares different ensemble methods for Sentiment analysis in Serbian language, as a low-resource language. No previous studies have experimented with ensemble methods in Serbian language and therefore this is a novel study. Dataset used in our experiment consists of movie reviews in Serbian language.
