Our experiment shows that ensemble of Large Language Models (LLMs) like BERT, RoBERTa, GPT-2, DistilBERT, that represent Transformers-based architecture and traditional models can boost the accuracy of the system in comparison with the base learners mentioned.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Origami Wideband 3D Printed Dielectric Resonator MIMO Antenna
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an origami-inspired, foldable, and packable wideband MIMO antenna, featuring a 3D-printed dielectric resonator. The proposed antenna offers physical reconfigurability of the radiation patterns, providing an additional degree of freedom to enhance the MIMO system’s multiplexing, diversity, and beamforming capabilities. Three folding states: 0° (unfolded), 45° fold, and 360° fold can be achieved with the proposed origami configurations. A stable gain ranging between 4 and 6.2 dBi is achieved across the operating frequency band of 8.7–12 GHz, with an efficiency > 90%. Last, we conducted experimental validation and observed strong agreement with the simulation results, demonstrating the potential of the proposed MIMO antenna as a unit cell for a massive MIMO system.

articleTitle: AI based Fault Diagnosis in Power Transformer-A Deep Learning Framework using Convolutional Neural Network based on Infrared Imaging and Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network tools
abstract: The condition of a transformer impacts the safety of electrical power networks. Transformer failures not only reduce system reliability but also cause serious accidents and financial losses. Various diagnostic techniques exist to monitor transformer operation, but most are challenging for real-time monitoring due to difficulty in online identification, noise interference, and high maintenance costs. This article proposes an overheating defect diagnosis method using forward-looking infrared (FLIR) thermography images and introduces a deep learning framework for power transformers. The proposed thermal camera system collects four types of FLIR images. Wasserstein Autoencoder Reconstruction (WAR) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) models have been used to process these images. The trained CNN and WAR models have been combined in series to form a defect diagnosis module. The aim is to develop a cost-effective monitoring approach using remotely captured thermal images of a power transformer in an outdoor substation. The CNN model has been used to process these images to extract detailed feature parameters, preventing incomplete information issues from various feature-extraction techniques. Transformer health is classified into four categories: Monitor, Likely Defect, Repair at the Next Opportunity, and Major Defect Repair Immediately, based on temperature rise above ambient. The combined WAR–CNN technique has been used to improve remote monitoring. This approach has resulted in identifying common defects with high accuracy and has offered significant benefits over state-of-the-art methods, compact storage needs, and high diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband Multi-mode Circular Patch Antenna for LEO Satellite Application
abstract: This study presents a novel broadband multi-mode circular patch antenna that incorporates loading shorting pins to enhance its operational capabilities. This innovative antenna has been meticulously developed to function through the excitation of various modes, thereby expanding its potential applications in modern communication systems. The structural design of the antenna comprises a circular patch, complemented by strategically positioned shorting pins, which have been specifically modified to facilitate the generation of diverse Transverse Magnetic (TM) modes. This modification allows for the achievement of distinct surface current distributions and corresponding radiation patterns. According to the simulation results obtained from comprehensive analyses, the half-power beamwidth of the antenna in the vertical plane exhibits a range of variation, specifically between 106 degrees and 110 degrees across the specified frequency band. Furthermore, owing to its ability to operate in multiple modes, the realized gain of the antenna showcases a notable variability, ranging from 2.44 dBi to 3.79 dBi. These findings underscore the antenna's potential for versatility in performance, making it a promising candidate for future wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: HealChain: Enhancing Security and Accessibility of Medical Records through Blockchain Technology
abstract: This paper introduces a blockchain-based system designed to enable secure sharing of medical records across different healthcare institutions. The proposed solution stores medical records off-chain to ensure scalability and efficient data management, while allowing patients to retain full control over their data. This approach also supports easier integration with existing health information systems. Smart contracts are utilized to automate critical functions such as user registration and document access control, ensuring that only authorized entities can access or modify records. We detail the methods used to protect data confidentiality, uphold patient privacy, and maintain the integrity of medical records. Additionally, we describe the system’s operational workflow. The system prototype was evaluated in terms of computational efficiency under varying transactional loads. The findings demonstrate the system’s potential as a secure and effective solution for medical record management, with the capability to integrate with existing healthcare infrastructures.

articleTitle: Speech Dereverberation Using U-Net and Minimum-Phase Inverse Prefiltering
abstract: Reverberation in enclosed spaces degrades audio quality, particularly in speech signals, due to the overlap of direct sound with reflected waves. This paper aims to investigate a method for improving U-Net efficiency by using minimum-phase prefiltering. The method is especially effective for environments with high RT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> values, and it can be applied in scenarios where the Room Impulse Response (RIR) has been estimated. It involves a U-Net architecture for non-linear filtering of the all-pass component of the RIR, using spectrograms as input and output. The proposed approach improves dereverberation performance and restores the clarity of audio signals.

articleTitle: Person re-identification with transformers and image stacking
abstract: Person re-identification (ReID) is increasingly important due to the expansion of surveillance cameras. ReID can effectively operate in various conditions, making it suitable for security, retail analytics, and smart city applications. We propose a transformer-based model, DeepChangeVIT-ReID, fine-tuned with triplet loss, using the DeepChange dataset. We address long-term ReID challenges, including pose variations, camera angle differences, and clothing alterations. DeepChangeVIT-ReID achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly improving Rank-1 accuracy compared to existing methods on the DeepChange dataset.

articleTitle: Modeling Communications in SoC and Co-simulation Analysis with IEEE 1666 SystemC
abstract: IEEE 1666 (SystemC) plays a vital role in system level design and verification of complex communication circuits along with several other modeling languages. It is capable of providing a powerful framework for modeling and simulating System on Chip (SoC) architectures, helping designers to explore system-level behaviour and optimise performance early in the development process. This paper carries out two primary investigations - first, it examines the differences in computation time while modeling circuits both simple and complex with Simulink and SystemC TDF (Timed Data Flow). The results show that SystemC TDF outpaces Simulink in terms of speed irrespective of the circuit complexity. The second investigation is a comparative study to analyse the ability of Matlab and Octave for co-simulation with SystemC. Co-simulation allows the integration of components in several domains along with high flexibility in system verification. The co-simulation flow starts with a sinusoidal source generated in Matlab which is used as an input source for a SystemC TDF module whose output is further post-processed in Matlab. In addition, similar investigations are done with Octave, using it for both post and pre-processing. The computational time in both cases are evaluated for each stages of the co-simulation flow and proves that Matlab is significantly faster than Octave in the investigated setups.

articleTitle: Implementation of JESD204B Receiver for Interleaved Analog to Digital Convertor in FPGA
abstract: With the continuously increasing frequency bands of signals in the world of electronics, new challenges in their processing constantly arise. This fact pushes both component manufacturers and their users to develop new methods to keep pace with these demands. One approach is to increase the conversion speed of traditional analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). Another possible solution is to use the time-interleaving technique, which employs an array of slower converters working in parallel. Modern ADCs, especially those operating in the range of units to tens of GSPS, feature the JESD204 communication standard, which transmits digitized data to the next system, typically an FPGA. Therefore, this system must implement a receiver for this standard, incorporating all necessary functionalities. We have designed and implemented a receiver for this standard for the FPGA circuit. Subsequently, the functionality and characteristics were verified on a real-time interleaved sampling system.

articleTitle: Leakage Rate Analysis of Untrusted RIS
abstract: This paper investigates the leakage-rate perfor¬mance of untrusted passive and absorptive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), which is controlled by the unauthorized users. In order to minimize the information leakage, the investigation also considers that untrusted passive and absorptive RIS is affected by a limited number of friendly jammers. The outage probability performance metric is considered for the investigation. Analytical derivations are approximated to asymptotic derivations and verified by means of Monte Carlo-based computer simulations. The obtained results indicate that friendly jammer degrades the performance of the passive and absorptive RIS when it has a small number of reflecting elements. However, as the number of reflecting elements increases, the resistance of the untrusted RIS improves, and the friendly jammer’s effects become negligible.

articleTitle: Secure Distributed Computing in Cloud Using Trusted Execution Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of integrating AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) technology into a distributed computing environment. Distributed computing frameworks are designed to handle large-scale data processing and complex computational tasks by distributing workloads across multiple nodes. However, ensuring the security and integrity of data in such environments, particularly in multi-tenant and cloud settings, poses a significant challenge. Confidential computing concepts and in particular AMD SEV address these concerns by providing virtual machine memory encryption and isolation, even protecting against threats from the hypervisor. This study evaluates the potential to set up distributed computing in the confidential computing settings. It will discuss current gaps and the performance overhead of using AMD SEV in distributed systems, focusing on task execution times and scalability. Experiments were conducted using different workloads studying performance impact. Results indicate that while SEV introduces additional data processing, the overall average performance impact is minimal, making it a viable solution for secure distributed processing without significant performance degradation.

articleTitle: Towards More Cyber-Physically Resilient Railways: Implications from the SAFETY4RAILS Project
abstract: This paper introduces a simulation setup within a cyber-physical system to monitor vehicles and railway infrastructure environments. It features an alert mechanism visualized in VR to enhance practitioners' awareness and preparedness for cyber-physical threats. Demonstrated in the European project SAFETY4RAILS, the study shares valuable lessons learned.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and the Future of Drowsy Driving Prevention
abstract: With the number of vehicles in use rising every year, drowsy driving crashes are becoming more prevalent than ever before. This study delves into the application of Artificial Intelligence in risk management; more explicitly, the use of deep learning in computer vision to detect if a driver is alert or in an unsafe position to operate a vehicle. Two AI models were used to train the dataset, those being YOLOv8-m and YOLOv9-gelan-c. YOLOv9-gelan-c is the most recent of the two computer vision models and the most advanced. However, YOLOv8-m was also used to set a benchmark for a consistent and efficient model. After a comparative overview, the YOLOv9-gelan-c model was chosen as the superior model due to its higher average AP scores (90.6% against 88.9%) and the lack of a false positive. These findings are essential for creating an effective drowsy driving prevention system. The model’s performance was also compared against several other studies that used computer vision and detection software. Furthermore, this research promotes the integration of detection software for safety features within the automotive industry, to lower drowsy driving accidents and fatalities.

articleTitle: A Method for Accelerating Encrypted Data Search in Laravel Applications Using a Coded Search Parameter
abstract: Efficiently searching encrypted data within web applications presents a significant challenge for software engineers, primarily because traditional search methods necessitate decrypting each record individually to check for matches, leading to considerable computational overhead. The authors in this paper introduce an optimized search methodology for encrypted data in Laravel web applications by implementing a Coded Search Parameter (CSP). By incorporating an additional attribute into the MySQL database entity, which stores a coded representation of the initial character of the encrypted data - we substantially reduce server resource consumption and search time. During the search process, the algorithm initially executes a query filtered by the CSP attribute value, effectively narrowing down potential matches before decrypting the now reduced set of records. This approach also ensures that personal data remains protected without compromising data security. In this paper we provide a detailed exposition of the CSP method's implementation, evaluate its impact on search efficiency and present performance improvement analyses compared to traditional encrypted data search methods. Based on the research findings, it is concluded that the CSP method in Laravel applications significantly reduces search time for encrypted data, achieving an average acceleration of 73.58%.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Parallel Electrocardiogram Compression Based on Successive Differences
abstract: We focus on parallelization methods for an electrocardiogram data compression algorithm based on successive differences to gain insights into the advantages and disadvantages of parallel implementations. The experimental methodology exposes a comprehensive and systematic benchmarking process with varying input file sizes, hosting machine characteristics, and two popular parallelization approaches: OpenMP and MPI. We check the research hypothesis to see if parallelizing the compression algorithm can reduce the runtime while keeping the original algorithm’s compression results. Our analysis and discussion show that OpenMP outperforms MPI. An OpenMP implementation with 12 threads on a processor with six cores achieves the highest average speedup of 7 versus a single-thread implementation. Performance gains depend heavily on the utilized hardware and the degree of parallelism.

articleTitle: Self-consistent problem of microwave radiation effects on layered structures with nanoconducting films using parallelization techniques
abstract: The paper presents the main provisions of the self-consistent problem on the effect of microwave electromagnetic radiation on layered structures with nanoconducting films. Computational results using parallelization technology in solving finite-difference equations are obtained.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Optimal Operation of Green Hydrogen Refueling
abstract: This study presents an AI-based optimized energy management model for a hydrogen refueling station with a PV system and fuel cell (FC). Using the Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE) model for day-ahead PV generation and electricity price forecasting, with real data from Spain, the station efficiently manages hydrogen demand and electricity sales. Despite lower-than-expected PV production (11,559.39 kWh vs. 12,991.71 kWh), real-time revenue rose to 1,144.84 Euros, demonstrating operational flexibility and profit.

articleTitle: Inverter performance analysis for building integrated oversized PV system
abstract: The building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems are a popular option for integrating renewable energy sources in the power system, and for users to reduce energy bills. This paper analyzes the performance of inverters in BIPV systems with oversized PV configurations. Oversizing PV systems has become a common practice to optimize energy production, particularly in periods of low sunlight, but it raises concerns about efficiency, power quality, and potential economic implications. Performance analysis is performed on two inverters, one operating under an overloaded regime due to the oversized PV installation and another under normal conditions. Several performance metrics are compared, including efficiency, thermal behavior, THD, and economic factors. The results demonstrate that although oversizing can slightly increase the inverter’s temperature and affect power quality, the efficiency was better for the overloaded inverter, although the investment costs have increased. These results offer practical insights for designing PV systems, showing that oversizing can be beneficial if properly managed.

articleTitle: A Co-design of AI Chatbots for Child Online Protection with Parents, Guardians and Caregivers
abstract: A challenge that many parents, guardians and caregivers face navigating parenthood in the digital era is the implement of online safety for their children. This research highlights the implementation of AI chatbots which has a promising outcome in the world of Child Online Protection. Humans’ fondness for conversations has allowed many users to ease into the utilization of AI chatbots for educational purposes. This research explored collaborative (co) design process with users. Thus, the AI chatbot named Gogo COPPAA was developed through collaborative work. By gathering data on the issues that parents face online has generated ideas for designing an application and chatbot that is of satisfactory use for its user. Further directions of the AI chatbot would be to have it tested on further platforms and have it widely accessible for parents, guardians and caregivers.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of Gas Sensors for Ammonia detection
abstract: With the rise of Industry 4.0, smart gas sensors have become indispensable tools across a wide range of sectors, including chemical industries, environmental monitoring, and healthcare. These sensors enable faster, more accurate, and autonomous detection of hazardous gases, enhancing both safety and operational efficiency in industrial processes. In this paper, we focus on the development of sensors for gas detection, with a particular emphasis on ammonia (NH3), a commonly used industrial gas that poses significant risks in the event of leaks. To address this, we designed a sensor based on a patch antenna with a cavity optimized to operate at a reference frequency of approximately 10 GHz. This design was chosen to maximize the sensor’s sensitivity to changes in gas concentration. Our initial tests produced promising results, demonstrating frequency shifts of 80 MHz, 240 MHz, and 320 MHz in response to NH3 concentrations of 10 ppm, 40 ppm, and 50 ppm, respectively.

articleTitle: Multivariate Statistical Analysis of Reflection Coefficients from Free Space Measurements of Saline Solutions
abstract: Salinity levels have a crucial impact on ecosystems, including plants, marine life, and agriculture. Antenna-based sensors are preferred over satellite remote sensing for salinity detection, as they are cost-effective, easy to deploy, and better suited for local measurements. This study employs a broadband horn antenna to measure the scattering parameters (S-parameters) of bottled water with varying salt content. The S-parameter results were evaluated using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). In PCA, the real and imaginary parts of the S-parameters were analyzed to reveal distinct differences between the salt concentrations. PC1 accounted for 58.5% and 66.54% of the variance for the real and imaginary parts of the S-parameters, respectively. Furthermore, the dataset, including the first derivatives of the real and imaginary of the S-parameters, was examined, with PC1 explaining 30.41% and 29.93% of the variance for the real and imaginary components, respectively. The reduced features obtained from PCA analysis can further be applied in machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Deep Neural Networks (DNN), for both regression and classification tasks. This process has the potential for accurately identifying salt concentrations in water through a microwave sensing system.

articleTitle: Ultrasound breast cancer image classification with GAN-based synthetic data augmentation
abstract: Ultrasound images are used in various branches of medicine to detect diseases. The process of obtaining this data is complex due to procedures and legal restrictions, leading to scarce datasets. Different data augmentation techniques can be employed to improve classification performance. This paper shows that augmenting the ultrasound breast cancer images dataset using generative adversarial networks (GANs) increased the classification accuracy compared to the original dataset and compared to the dataset augmented using standard techniques.

articleTitle: A Robust Approach to Integrating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems with In-Vehicle Infotainment
abstract: Fundamental elements of system design include strategies for achieving optimal performance and stability, especially in software for electric vehicles (EVs). Guided by the ISO 26262 standard, automotive systems are positioned to meet safety requirements. This paper explores the communication between two rapidly advancing automotive domains, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI), with a focus on ensuring secure integration and synchronization while considering the trade-offs between safety and overall system performance.

articleTitle: Magnetic Flux Density Harmonics Estimation in the Vicinity of the Overhead Lines Utilizing Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a method based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for magnetic flux density harmonics estimation in the vicinity of overhead lines. The proposed method can be employed for the magnetic flux density estimation in the cases of excitation currents with a pure sinusoidal waveform, as well as for excitation currents with harmonically distorted waveforms. The method utilizes two ANNs that are trained in a such way that enables their application for overhead lines of arbitrary phase conductor configurations and arbitrary current harmonic spectrum. In this paper, the proposed method is applied for magnetic flux density harmonics estimation in the vicinity of a typical distribution overhead line. The proposed method is validated by comparison with Biot-Savart based method. The obtained results demonstrate not only the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method but also the importance of considering the magnetic flux density harmonics in the vicinity of power facilities.

articleTitle: Frequency sampling scheme for effective MIMO-OFDM channel estimation with SALSA and LS algorithms
abstract: In this paper we consider the channel estimation problem in MIMO-OFDM system, when the base station has a hybrid architecture of antenna array. Considering uplink CE, overhead reduction for pilot resources in time/frequency OFDM grid was studied. Utilizing properties of channel decomposition via sum of Kronecker product factors and applying Tucker format decomposition for every decomposition term, SALSA (Sequential Alternating Least Squares Approximation) algorithm was applied for partial channel tensor reconstruction on regularly measured sub-carrier frequencies. LS (Least Square) algorithm was used to reconstruct the whole channel tensor after partial channel tensor estimation at comb frequencies. Additionally, we investigated schemes where sub-carriers set is different for different OFDM symbols. It was shown that significant reduction of pilot sub-carriers can be achieved while keeping good accuracy of CE if positions of regular sampling patterns with large period are shifted in frequency during multiple consecutive symbols. Simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed method of channel estimation by SALSA and LS algorithms in comparison with fixed set of sub-carriers.

articleTitle: HFSWR Input Data Visualization and Multi-Target Simulation
abstract: Signal processing in High Frequency Surface Wave Radars is a complex task whether it is primary signal processing or tracking. As a final result, the radar output data (detection and track files) are generated. These data can be used to evaluate radar performance, by comparison with Automatic Identification System data. In this paper, we present a user - friendly simulator used to visualize output radar data, as well as a multi-target simulator that enables users to create random ship trajectories by setting all relevant parameters. The paper contains the detailed simulator description, two proposed multi-target simulation models, and simulation results that were inserted into experimentally obtained radar data. The results show that it is possible to generate any trajectory in fully controllable scenario. There is a significant level of demand for such a simulator, as it offers possibility of testing scenarios that may be challenging to encounter in real-world and therefore help with the design of various applications in this demanding field.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Learning Networks Performance By Using B-Spline Activation Functions for Clutter Removal in GPR
abstract: Traditional clutter removal methods struggle with complex clutter and multiple targets in Ground-Penetrating Radar images. This study proposes using B-spline activation functions in the deep-learning models to improve clutter removal in GPR. Experimental results demonstrate that B-spline-enhanced models outperform their ReLU-based counterparts, with improvements of up to 2.20% in PSNR, 0.035% in MS-SSIM, and 15.83% in SCR, showcasing their potential for real-world GPR applications.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Data Augmentation Techniques on Emotional Speech Recognition
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are known to perform poorly in recognition of atypical speech, which certainly includes emotional speech. The labor-intensive nature of developing comprehensive speech databases for training purposes has led to the widespread adoption of synthetic speech data generation, utilizing existing natural speech, in numerous research studies. This paper examines the impact of standard data augmentation techniques, including pitch shifting, time stretching and volume adjustment on the accuracy of isolated-word recognizer of emotional speech. The experiments carried out indicate a significant increase in accuracy achieved through a single augmentation based on pitch-shifting for all emotional states.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Physical Layer Authentication Method for Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
abstract: As Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) find increasing utility in security, monitoring, and exploration applications, robust node authentication becomes crucial. We propose a novel physical-layer cooperative authentication method using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that leverages spatial dependency of underwater acoustic channels. Our two-stage framework first allows trusted nodes to collect signals and learn unique channel characteristics from authorized transmitters through CNN-based analysis of channel impulse responses (CIRs). In the online stage, trained models authenticate incoming signals in real-time, with a central sink node combining inputs from multiple trusted nodes to enhance resilience against localized attacks. Bellhop simulations show that the proposed CNN-based method accurately detects malicious packets, outperforming SVM approach that relies on standard authentication features.

articleTitle: Forecasting Solar Energy Substation Voltages Using Metaheuristic Optimized GRU
abstract: As global energy demand grows, renewable sources offer a key alternative to fossil fuels. However, integrating these sources into power grids presents challenges, especially with supply unpredictability. This paper demonstrates how AI, specifically using a modified PSO algorithm to enhance GRU models, can predict solar energy output and improve grid balancing. Experiments on public datasets show that the optimized models achieve high accuracy, with the best models demonstrating a mean square error (MSE) of 0.024642 and an mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.000943 in hourly predictions, facilitating renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Classification of Lyric Poetry Written in Serbian
abstract: In terms of natural language processing, Serbian belongs to low-resource languages, with a small number of available datasets and tools. In this paper, we present a novel poem classification corpus in the Serbian language, in multi-label and multiclass variants. We provide an analysis of this dataset and then use it to train and evaluate machine learning classifiers, ranging from simple linear ones to multiple large language model variants.

articleTitle: Performance Measurement Testbed for Hybrid Access Based on Multipath Transport Layer Protocol
abstract: Modern communication devices usually have multiple network interfaces allowing them to communicate over different networking technologies. This property is especially interesting in mobile communications, where hybrid terrestrial/satellite access can be utilized to achieve more reliable communication, increased bandwidth and continuous service sessions. Protocols that support multipath are necessary to achieve hybrid access. MultiPath Transmission Control Protocol (MPTCP) is one such protocol that is even recognized by 5G standards as one of promising approaches to support hybrid access. In this paper, we propose initial testbed for measuring MPTCP performances to be used in estimating the performance of hybrid access.

articleTitle: On the Bit Error Probability of DMA-Based Systems
abstract: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) are an alternative application of metasurfaces as active reconfigurable antennas with advanced analog signal processing and beamforming capabilities, which have been proposed to replace conventional antenna arrays for next-generation transceivers. Motivated by this, we investigate the bit error probability (BEP) optimization in a DMA-based system, propose an iterative optimization algorithm, which adjusts the transmit precoder and the weights of the DMA elements, prove its convergence and derive complexity.

articleTitle: Towards Formal Verification of Federated Learning Orchestration Protocols on Satellites
abstract: Python Testbed for Federated Learning Algorithms (PTB-FLA) is a simple FL framework targeting edge systems that implements both centralized and decentralized FL orchestration protocols, which were formally verified in a previous paper using the process algebra CSP. This approach is appropriate for systems with stationary nodes but cannot be applied to systems with moving nodes. In this paper, we use celestial mechanics to model spacecraft movement, and timed automata (TA) to formalize and verify the centralized FL orchestration protocol, in two phases. In the first phase, we created a conventional TA model to prove traditional properties, namely deadlock freeness and termination. In the second phase, we created a stochastic TA model to prove timing correctness and to estimate termination probability.

articleTitle: Square Patch Antenna with Ferrite Wall
abstract: Microstrip (patch) antennas exhibit significant parasitic radiation in horizontal directions, which deteriorates antenna performance. Reduction of this parasitic radiation has been an important, but challenging task. In [1], this radiation for a circular patch is suppressed by a ferrite ring (a wall), which encircles the antenna. Our goals are to use numerical modeling to (a) investigate if a similar wall can be designed for a square patch antenna and (b) identify physical mechanisms that are behind this technique. The main results are new local optima with narrower walls than in [1].

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Fractional-order Models of Battery Cells Utilizing Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: In this paper the parameter estimation of five fractional-order models of a battery cell is performed. Real measurements obtained by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy on a lithium cobalt oxide graphite cell are utilized, although the method can be applied to cells of various battery types. Optimal parameter values are determined by minimizing the sum of squared residuals, where the residual is defined as the distance between measured and estimated impedance values in the complex plane for a specified frequency, with the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm employed. The obtained results are compared and analyzed. This approach could be part of a broader process aimed at improving the performance of individual battery cells of various battery types and, consequently, the overall battery.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Coffee Odor Identification and Classification
abstract: The development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology and Machine Learning (ML) techniques led to the appearance of systems that can detect and identify odors, known as electronic noses. In this context, the present paper proposes an intelligent system for the identification and classification of odors emitted by different types of coffee, based on the Bosch BME688 gas sensor development kit and on a software application with ML capabilities. The system architecture particularities are shown, and several tests to evaluate the system performance are described.

articleTitle: On the Computational Determination of the Third Focus of the Cartesian Oval
abstract: In this paper, the correctness of the algebraic determination of the coordinate of the third focus of the Cartesian oval is examined and analysed. This analysis is necessary because the process includes solving systems with a large number of multivariate polynomial equations using the computer algebra system Maple. The paper also considers the difficulties and limitations of using computers in determining the coordinate of the third focus.

articleTitle: The impact of inverse matrix computation on the results of the Capon algorithm
abstract: Algorithms for estimating the direction of signal arrival are crucial in various applications, particularly in acoustics. They are essential for accurately locating sources of both desired and undesired sound signals. This research focuses on the performance analysis of the Capon algorithm using an approximated inverse covariance matrix. Instead of using direct methods for matrix inversion, iterative methods are employed, potentially leading to shorter processing times and reduced memory usage. Furthermore, the performance of these iterative methods is compared to the direct Cholesky method in terms of computational operations.

articleTitle: Comparative review of the surround speaker virtualizers on DSP platform
abstract: This paper reviews three DSP-based audio virtualizer implementations used in immersive audio technologies, which have transformed sound experiences with limited speaker setups. Focusing on key parameters such as memory usage, processing power, and input/output layouts, the study employs multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approach to evaluate each virtualizer's strengths and trade-offs. The findings provide insights into the efficiency and feasibility of these virtualizers in delivering high-quality immersive audio in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Optimal Selection of Locations for Wheat Ear Smartphone Sampling Using UAV Multispectral Data
abstract: This research aims to improve the smartphone image acquisition procedure for wheat yield prediction involving the non-uniformity of wheat fields in the final yield prediction. We compare two image acquisition methods—random smartphone sampling and a proposed optimized approach—using UAV multispectral data. The data was obtained from a DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral, collected in mid-May and June from two wheat fields in Vojvodina: Kovilj and Šajkaš. The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index were used to segment fields into four management zones. The median value of the Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index for each zone and the nearest location in terms of distance from the median point represent optimal locations. At these locations, wheat ears were sampled to estimate yield. The results demonstrate that the optimized approach provides a more efficient and reliable method, leading to significant time savings and ensuring precise early wheat yield predictions. At the optimal locations in both fields, the yield estimates are consistently underestimated compared to the actual yield, while at the randomly selected locations, the yield is generally overestimated, with underestimation occurring in only one case. The strong correlation between the Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index and wheat yield, averaging 0.89 (0.88 for Kovilj and 0.90 for Šajkaš), underscoring the effectiveness of the proposed method in identifying areas with greater productivity potential.

articleTitle: Steam players count prediction using GRU optimized by modified PSO
abstract: Accurate prediction of Steam players count is vital for efficient resource management, informed decision-making, and ability to maximize the potential of each game over its entire lifecycle. From the business point of view, this can directly affect profitability, player retention and strategic planning. This paper examines potential of GRU tuned by an improved version of renowned particle swarm optimization algorithm. The proposed model was placed into comparative simulations with other potent optimization techniques, and obtained experimental outcomes clearly pointed out the supreme performance of the suggested technique.

articleTitle: An approach to Wavelet-Hermite image representation
abstract: The paper proposes a Wavelet-Hermite approach for image representation. The wavelet transform is applied at one or two levels to achieve a certain level of compression, followed by the Hermite transform representation using a reduced number of Hermite functions. The Hermite transform, gained attention in recent years, offering advantages over traditional methods such as the Fourier or discrete cosine transforms for image analysis. With this approach, a one-dimensional Hermite transform is combined with two-dimensional wavelet decomposition. This method can be applied for both image compression and noise reduction, leveraging the Hermite transform’s efficiency in noisy environments. The proposed theory is validated experimentally, and image quality is measured using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio.

articleTitle: FMCW and OFDM radar receiver SW tool for performance analysis in automotive applications
abstract: In this work, we present a software simulator of automotive radar receivers for Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signals operating in the currently used 76-81 GHz frequency band as well as in the D-band (110-170 GHz) allocation, defined for the future in Europe. The simulator has been designed and implemented for evaluating the effects of interfering systems in realistic traffic scenarios, as a function of the configuration parameters of the automotive radar sensors. We present and discuss the effects on the Signal to Noise pluse Interferer Ratio (SNIR), assuming that both the interferer and the interfered use either FMCW or OFDM signals.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Wavelength Monitoring System
abstract: In this paper a directional optical coupler is modeled in OptiBPM software. The influence of coupling length on the power on coupler outputs is investigated. Afterwards, modeled optical coupler is deployed as a part of wavelength monitoring system in OptiSystem software. The wavelength monitoring system output modeled using OptiSystem and OptiBPM is compared with the experimental data obtained with the implemented wavelength monitoring system.

articleTitle: Design of Measuring and Power Circuits for Induction Flowmeters
abstract: This paper focuses on the design and implementation of detection circuits for induction flowmeters, including excitation circuits that generate electromagnetic fields. The described detection circuits are categorized into signal modifying circuits, signal digitization circuits, and circuits utilizing optical detection of the flowing medium. The output of these subcomponents is intended for integration into an innovative flowmeter designed to measure very small flow rates of carbonated beverages.

articleTitle: DuoBrain-HVAC: A Hybrid Autonomous Agent for Controlling HVAC Systems
abstract: The HVAC system consumes a significant portion of building energy, contributing to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. This paper presents DuoBrain-HVAC, a hybrid deep reinforcement learning agent, designed to optimize energy use by controlling a discrete (ON/OFF) air handling unit and a continuous (temperature setpoint) actuator. Simulated in an amphitheater using EnergyPlus, the hybrid agent combines DDQN and TD3 algorithms, achieving faster convergence and reducing energy consumption by 23.68% compared to DDQN and 16.24% compared to TD3.

articleTitle: Analysis and Detection of Blueberry Fruits for Smart Agriculture
abstract: Smart agriculture introduces various technological means and approaches to achieve the highest possible yields and simultaneously control the chemical integrity of the fruits themselves. In this paper, image processing techniques are applied for the analysis of blueberry fruits to obtain the most significant information about them. The blueberry detector, primarily based on color features, was applied to the recorded video sequences. Here, the detection rate of 89% was achieved in the case of ripe blueberries, and 86% in the case of unripe ones.

articleTitle: CO2 Emission and Fuel Consumption Effects in VANETs: a Simulation Analysis Using SUMO
abstract: In this paper, the Urban Mobility Simulation software (SUMO) is used to analyze vehicle emissions and fuel consumption. The analysis is conducted in scenarios generated with OpenStreetMap (OSM) Web Wizard, using predefined configurations and varying vehicle characteristics, including different types of vehicles and driving styles. The results reveal that the use of quick configurations may introduce inaccuracies in the metrics, negatively impacting the precision of studies related to traffic and air pollution.

articleTitle: Possibility of Applying the EEBUS to the IoT Based Renewable Energy Sources Powered Station for Electric Vehicles Charging
abstract: Electric vehicles market share is increasing rapidly. This trend has resulted in a huge demand for residential and commercial renewable energy powered charging stations for electric vehicles. The stations that have been installed can be integrated into a smart city environment to boost station usage, save energy and money, and improve community quality of life. In this paper, we propose IoT based renewable energy sources powered station for electric vehicles charging which uses EEBUS based communication model. The proposed architecture and communication model aim to standardize the integration of stations into smart city concept. In this way, the interoperability challenges would be considerably decreased and the integration process would be easier, cheaper and faster.

articleTitle: ML-based Short Physical Performance Battery future score prediction based on questionnaire data
abstract: Effective slowing down of older adults’ physical capacity deterioration requires intervention as soon as the first symptoms surface. In this paper, we analyze the possibility of predicting the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score at a four-year horizon based on questionnaire data. The ML algorithms tested included Random Forest, XGBoost, Linear Regression, dense and TabNet neural networks. The best results were achieved for the XGBoost (mean absolute error of 0.79 points). Based on the Shapley values analysis, we selected smaller subsets of features (from 10 to 20) and retrained the XGBoost regressor, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.82.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep-Learning Based Method for Cell Phenotype Classification
abstract: Cell phenotype classification represents a crucial task in various medical and biological applications. With fluorescent microscopy emerging as a leading method for biological cell characteristics analysis, cell phenotype classification is often being performed by analysing fluorescence images. This paper proposes a novel approach for performing single-cell classification in a sequence of several preprocessing sub-steps, relevant feature extraction, and a deep learning model for performing the final classification. Due to the lack of relevant publicly available datasets, the algorithm was tested on artificially generated images, obtained by the authors’ own previously developed artificial data generation system. Very promising performance metrics were obtained, testifying to the utility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Convolutional Networks Using a Modified Metaheuristic for Apple Tree Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: The global demand for food is continuously increasing. The use of artificial intelligence can vastly improve the field of agriculture. Computer vision can help detect issues with crops. This work focuses on detecting plant diseases in apple tree leaves through the analysis of images. The proposed approach consists of a convolutional neural network (CNN) optimized by a hybrid optimization algorithm. The optimized models showcase favorable outcomes with the best models attaining an accuracy of 0.772408.

articleTitle: Big Data System For Cable Operator Network Performance Monitoring
abstract: Nowadays, internet use is deeply rooted in all aspects of human society. From entertainment, gaming, and leisure to digitalized e-government services, education, and national defense, from children to the elderly population, this service is present everywhere for everyone. High demand and high competition among internet providers force continuous improvement of their networks. To analyze network performance and be able to react proactively, operators need to collect performance measurements from their devices. Considering the number of devices, network heterogeneity, data volume, and many other aspects, this can be a very challenging job. This paper presents a system for big data collection and performance monitoring implemented for cable networks. The introduced system solves all the mentioned challenges while being scalable enough to give unlimited capacity and processing power, with a flexible design that can be easily adjusted to support many other use cases. Although this system is presented through a cable network use case, the same can be used in other networks as well.

articleTitle: Determining category metadata in open data portals – an approach based on Formal Concept Analysis
abstract: The efforts for data transparency and open government initiatives have resulted in a large amount of data being published on open data portals. These portals are organized to enhance published data accessibility by providing search mechanisms that utilize metadata such as category, tags, format, and publisher. However, due to the metadata incompleteness, such as missing category information, datasets are harder to find. Therefore, within this paper, we address the issue of missing category information by proposing an approach for categorizing datasets using keywords and their usage within categories. The presented approach is based on the Formal Concept Analysis method, which is used to create a hierarchical order of keywords grounded on their usage within categories on one open data portal. Further, we present the evaluation of the presented method using data from the Canadian open data portal.

articleTitle: An insight into the visual sampling strategy: eye-tracking features in dyslexia
abstract: Dyslexia is neurological disorder that negatively impacts a person’s ability to read and comprehend textual content. It has varying estimations of prevalence ranging from 5 to 20% of the population, and an early diagnosis is fundamental for a timely intervention. One of the methods that is available for objective reading assessment and therefore contributes to the monitoring of dyslexic tendencies is eye-tracking. Using this technology, it is possible to obtain a better understanding of a person’s reading patterns, or visual attention patterns in general, and thus aid in the diagnostic process as well as the improvements obtained through therapy. In this paper, an introduction to the dyslexia definitions and diagnostic process is given, followed by a review of patterns obtained from eye-tracking for the purpose of dyslexia assessment. The overview of the different features shows the different approaches and their relation to spatial and temporal gaze characteristics as well as their sensitivity to gaze outliers and the total length of the text that is read. The experimental setups are discussed as well, discussing different types of stimuli and their influence. A discussion of different instrumentation, as well as technical requirements that can impact the quality of the obtained features is also discussed, alongside other aspects that can influence feature quality and therefore conclusions that can be drawn from them. Finally, directions for future work related to eye-tracking and dyslexia are given, considering the work presented in the literature and the development of new technologies.

articleTitle: System for remote control of electric vehicles charging stations powered by renewable energy sources
abstract: The trend of increasing the number of electric vehicles (EV) requires the installation of charging stations for electric vehicles. On the other hand, the concept of smart cities aims to increase the quality of life of citizens. This paper describes a system for remote control of charging stations for electric vehicles powered by renewable energy sources. The architecture of the system for remote control of the mentioned stations is described. The introduction of IoT into the station was also discussed in order to integrate it into the IoT system of the smart city. The telecommunication aspects were generally presented and it was shown why and how IoT is introduced into the EV charging station. The terminal for remote control of the station, as a central part of the system, is specially described. The terminal enables remote control of electric vehicle chargers, smart batteries and renewable energy sources, smart meters and fiscal cash registers. This paper also describes the realization of the hardware and software of such a terminal. Also, the application of artificial intelligence in the operation of the terminal was considered.

articleTitle: Detecting Hot Code from Partially Context-Sensitive Profiles
abstract: In order to achieve the peek program performance, compilers employ numerous optimizations. Some of these optimizations, although highly effective, come with the high price in terms of compilation time, and the compiled code size. This is why it is beneficial to apply optimizations on only selected portions of the most frequently executed code – hot code. In JIT-compiled programs, information about the frequency of code execution is available during the compilation, however, AOT compilers must compensate through the profiling data collected from the previous program runs. In this paper, we use partially context-sensitive profiles, for efficient profile collection and managing, to identify and reconstruct significant hot-code fragments. We show that, with the proper identification of the hot code, significantly better program performance can be achieved with reasonable cost.

articleTitle: Analysis of Massive IoT Networks in Nearest and Macro Diversity Reception Regime
abstract: In this overview paper, we present a reliability analysis for massive Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity in cellular networks. In such networks, IoT devices intermittently and unpredictably transmit short data packets to base stations (BSs), often causing interference with other devices sharing the same uplink channel. Assuming a slotted ALOHA random access scheme under Nakagami fading, we investigate the probability that a short-packet transmission from an IoT device fails to be decoded, in the nearest BS and macro diversity reception regime. Using a combination of finite block-length (FBL) information theory and stochastic geometry, we derive error probability expressions. These FBL-based results are compared with existing asymptotic expressions, which assume the transmission of asymptotically long packets. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the derived expressions and their relevance to the design and performance evaluation of massive IoT systems across a wide range of parameters.

articleTitle: IntelliLung AI-DSS Trustworthiness Evaluation Framework
abstract: The Artificial Intelligence Act was adopted in the European Parliament in March 2024 to establish a uniform legal framework for the development and uptake of human-centric and trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) in Europe. Considering that AI may generate risks and cause harm, the approach for evaluating the newly developed AI and decision support systems (DSS) will vary from domain to domain. This paper presents the approach the European Union (EU) funded project IntelliLung is currently implementing in the healthcare domain. The IEC 62559-2:2015 methodology was used to structure the IntelliLung AI-DSS requirements and define key performance indicators relevant for the functional parts of the system (data integration, pre-processing, AI modelling). "Ethics-by-design" and "Transparent AI design" methodologies have been used for the IntelliLung AI-DSS implementation. The compliance requirements analysis has shown that the trustworthiness of AI-DSS relies on a wide set of measures including information and communication security, explainable AI algorithms, data governance and privacy considerations, as well as risk-management throughout the entire lifecycle of AI-DSS as a high-risk AI system.

articleTitle: The Future of Maritime Target Detection Using HFSWRs: High-Resolution Approach
abstract: In recent years, maritime surveillance of sea targets at long distances has been a current topic, especially from a security point of view. For this purpose, High-Frequency Surface Wave Radars (HFSWRs) are often used because their detection range exceeds the over-the-horizon distance. This paper represents a comprehensive study of high-resolution (HR) primary signal processing in HFSWRs which is a critical task because the performance of such systems depends on it. The paper also proposes main principles of maritime target detection using HR approach, which differs from state-of-the art approaches. The proposed algorithms are based on a HR estimation of the Range–Doppler map, where target detection is performed, and then the azimuth estimation by a high-resolution MUSIC-type algorithm, that is executed for all detections founded in the range-Doppler map. The operation at one frequency, as well as bi-frequency operation mode are shown. The goal of the bi-frequency mode of operation is to improve the detectability of sea targets, which are affected by different Bragg-line interference patterns. The experimental study shows the effectiveness and efficiency of the newly developed algorithms in real conditions and promising performance that either matches or outperforms primary signal processing used by many existing radars. Probability of target detection, detection accuracy, matching with Automatic Identification System (AIS) and resolvability of targets are improved, which indicates that the proposed algorithms represent the future direction in HFSWR primary signal processing.
